description: Japchae is a vibrant and flavorful Korean dish featuring slippery sweet potato glass noodles stir-fried with an assortment of colorful vegetables and often thinly sliced meat. This classic dish offers a delightful balance of savory, sweet, and umami flavors, making it a beloved staple in Korean cuisine. It's perfect as a side dish, appetizer, or a light main course, enjoyed by all ages.

instructions.title: Prepare the Ingredients
instructions.text: Rehydrate the sweet potato glass noodles by soaking them in warm water for 30 minutes, then boil in fresh water for 7-8 minutes until translucent and chewy. Drain, rinse with cold water, and cut into shorter lengths (about 6-8 inches) with kitchen shears. Toss with 1 tablespoon of sesame oil to prevent sticking. Marinate the thinly sliced beef with 1 tablespoon soy sauce, 1 teaspoon sugar, 1/2 teaspoon minced garlic, and a pinch of black pepper for at least 10 minutes. Blanch spinach quickly in boiling water, squeeze out excess water, and season with 1 teaspoon soy sauce and 1 teaspoon sesame oil.

instructions.title: Cook Vegetables Separately
instructions.text: Heat 1 tablespoon of vegetable oil in a large pan or wok. Stir-fry the julienned carrots until slightly tender, about 2-3 minutes. Remove and set aside. In the same pan, stir-fry the sliced onions until translucent, about 2 minutes. Remove and set aside. Next, stir-fry the sliced shiitake mushrooms until tender and fragrant, about 3-4 minutes. Remove and set aside. Finally, quickly stir-fry the julienned red bell pepper for 1-2 minutes until slightly tender-crisp. Remove and set aside.

instructions.title: Cook the Beef
instructions.text: Add a little more vegetable oil to the pan if needed. Stir-fry the marinated beef until fully cooked and browned, about 3-4 minutes. Break up any clumps as it cooks. Once cooked, remove the beef from the pan and set it aside with the other cooked ingredients.

instructions.title: Combine and Season Noodles
instructions.text: In the same large pan or wok, add the cooked sweet potato glass noodles. Add 3 tablespoons of soy sauce, 1 tablespoon of sugar, and 1 tablespoon of minced garlic to the noodles. Stir-fry over medium heat for 2-3 minutes, ensuring the noodles are evenly coated and absorb the seasoning. The noodles should become shiny and slightly caramelized.

instructions.title: Mix All Components
instructions.text: Add all the cooked vegetables (spinach, carrots, onions, mushrooms, red bell pepper) and the cooked beef to the pan with the seasoned noodles. Add 2 tablespoons of sesame oil and 1 tablespoon of toasted sesame seeds. Using tongs or your hands (wearing gloves is recommended for better mixing), gently toss all the ingredients together until thoroughly combined. Ensure the seasoning is evenly distributed and all components are well incorporated.

instructions.title: Taste and Serve
instructions.text: Taste the Japchae and adjust seasoning if necessary. You might add a little more soy sauce, sugar, or sesame oil to your preference. Serve the Japchae warm or at room temperature, garnished with additional toasted sesame seeds. It makes a fantastic side dish or a light main course.

tips: For perfectly chewy noodles, do not overcook them. A quick rinse in cold water after boiling helps stop the cooking process and prevents sticking.
Cook vegetables and meat separately to maintain their distinct textures and flavors. This also prevents overcrowding the pan, which can lead to steaming instead of stir-frying.
Japchae is traditionally served at room temperature, making it an excellent dish for potlucks or meal prep. Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days.
